sections.title: What separates a useful chatbot from a frustrating one

blocks.heading: Grounded in your knowledge
paragraphs: Answers are retrieved from your own documents and data, not improvised by the model, which reduces hallucination and keeps answers consistent with policy.

blocks.heading: Integrations do the real work
paragraphs: Most of the value — and most of the cost — comes from integrations: CRM and ERP access, order management, scheduling and ticketing. We scope each integration explicitly.

blocks.heading: Guardrails and human handoff
paragraphs: Bots stay within defined topics, validate outputs and escalate to a person with the conversation history when they cannot help or a customer asks.

items.question: How much does AI chatbot development cost?
items.answer: AI chatbot development ranges from $8,000 for a basic FAQ bot to $200,000+ for an enterprise omnichannel platform. Most mid-complexity projects — a customer service bot with CRM integration, an internal knowledge assistant or a sales qualification bot — fall in the $25,000–$80,000 range.

items.question: What does a chatbot cost to run after launch?
items.answer: Ongoing costs include LLM API usage ($2,400–$18,000 per year), knowledge base maintenance ($5,000–$15,000 per year) and monitoring and support ($3,000–$8,000 per year), depending on volume and scope.

items.question: Can the chatbot take actions, not just answer questions?
items.answer: Yes. With CRM, ERP or order-management integrations, chatbots can look up and update records, create tickets and schedule meetings — with permissions and confirmation steps defined per action.

items.question: How do you stop the chatbot from making things up?
items.answer: We ground answers in retrieved content from your knowledge base, restrict the bot to defined topics, validate outputs and route uncertain cases to a person.

items.question: Which channels can the chatbot run on?
items.answer: Website chat widgets, Slack and Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp and other messaging channels, or all of them through an omnichannel platform.

items.question: Who owns the chatbot?
items.answer: You do — code, prompts, knowledge base pipelines and documentation are transferred at completion.

sections.heading: Scope a chatbot that actually resolves requests
sections.text: Tell us who the chatbot will serve and which systems it needs to reach. An engineer will reply within one business day with an approach and budget range.
